newsitem.title: MEXICO: Ahmsa Q1 results promising for yr - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Ahmsa Q1 results promising for yr - analysts.

text.p: Mexican steel company Altos Hornos de Mexico (Ahmsa) should see its margins improve for the rest of the year, analysts said on Wednesday after Ahmsa reported first quarter earnings that reflected growing internal demand.
Although the company reported an operating margin for the period of 16.3 percent, down from the first quarter in 1996 of 21.2 percent, analysts said operating margins were still encouraging.

"Last year, the peso's devaluation gave margins an artificial push. This year is more realistic and gives us the security that margins (for the year) will remain above 16.5 percent," Yvonne Delgadillo of Serfin Securities said, anticipating improved margins in future quarters.
She cited greater demand in the low-income housing market as boosting sales, while Ahmsa's new coal-injection blast furnace should reduce its vulnerability to fuel prices.
Five-year high natural gas prices in the winter months reportedly cut into first-quarter earnings.
Ahmsa noted that a 12 percent decrease in the average price of steel in international markets also cut into margins and earnings for the quarter.
Earnings per share for the first three months of 1997 came in at 1.94 pesos, compared with an average estimate from three analysts surveyed by Reuters of 1.82 pesos.

Ahmsa's net earnings dropped by about half to 754 million pesos from the quarter, compared to 1.541 billion pesos the previous year. Ahmsa attributed the decline partly to an appreciation of the peso in real terms.
Analysts said the company should continue to move toward more value-added products, a stated goal of the company.
"The company's new painting line is expected to become operational in the second quarter of 1997, increasing production of higher-margin, 'value-added' products," Ahmsa said in its earnings report.
Ahmsa said its finished product output grew 6.3 percent to 741,097 tonnes for the quarter, and liquid steel production grew 2.5 percent to 893,741 tonnes.
The company directed more of its sales to the domestic market, with 85 percent of product sold nationally, BBV-Probursa analyst Mexico City Jose Buendia said.
A recovering domestic economy will offer the company a more cost effective market for its goods, analysts said.
"As domestic demand in the construction and automobile sectors increases, Ahmsa's sales volume in the local market has also risen," Valores Finamex Mexico City analyst Chris Albi said.
Concerns about the company's debt level, about $1.5 billion at the end of 1996, should dissolve with pending debt issues and improving sales, analysts said.

Ahmsa has said it plans to issue a $200 Yankee bond soon. The company on Wednesday signed a two-tranche $330 million export-backed credit, with $140 million to refinance other export-backed debt and $190 to refinance dollar-denomiinated debt.
"Investors had been concerned over the company's leverage. It fell in the first quarter to 129 percent from 145 percent a year ago," Buendia said.
Ahmsa's debt level may remain a concern, however.
"Refinancing is positive because of lower interest cost, but you always have to remember the company's $1.5 billion debt," Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Mexico City analyst Leonardo Simpser said.
Simpser added the company has still not been able to make a delayed equity offering. Ahmsa has said it is waiting for more favorable market conditions.
((-- Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7903))
